Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: James Cook (author, Wikidata Q7324), died 1779. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Cook, James, 1728-1779") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: The American coast pilot [microform] : containing the courses and distances between the principal harbours, capes and headlands, from Passamaquoddy, through the Gulf of Florida : with directions for sailing into the same, describing the soundings, bearings of the light-houses and beacons from the rocks, shoals, ledges, &c. : together with the courses and distances from Cape Cod and Cape Ann to Georges' Bank, through the south and east channels, and the setting of the currents with latitudes and longitudes of the principal harbours on the coast, together with a tide table, Newburyport, Mass. : Printed by Edmund M. Blunt ..., 1804, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/cihm_35498. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 76%, 82%, 84% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of James Cook, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
